title: JSW Dulux Ltd - 500710 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: JSW Dulux Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.8% to ₹965 crore on ~25% volume growth, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.9% with PAT lifted by one-offs.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 18.8% like-to-like to ₹965 crore, with volume up about 25% (about 18-19% after price). Gross margin was 37.4%, which management says was depressed by roughly 2 points of high-cost inventory and about 2.5 points from reclassifying promotional spends to gross revenue; underlying gross margin was put at 39.5-40%. EBITDA rose 14.7% to ₹115.1 crore but margin diluted about 50 bps to 11.9% after headcount additions (~160 people) and R&D investment. Reported PAT of ₹135.5 crore includes one-offs: ₹55.9 crore dividend from ICICI R&T and ₹108 crore income tax refund (incl. ₹21.5 crore interest) for AY 2013-14.

financial_highlights.change: Management: underlying ~39.5-40% before inventory and reclassification effects
Other income; linked to real estate monetisation

segments.name: Decorative
segments.commentary: Grew double digits (management cites ~20% volume growth) and is ~60% of business; premium is ~45% of decorative and led growth, with premium and luxury growing high double digits. Mass and economy grew lower.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: All sub-segments grew upwards of 25%; automotive grew strongly with premium OEM and refinish wins (Porsche, Mahindra, MG via JSW group, Sikkens body shops).

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected in 13-15% range going forward, as reinvestment costs normalise and input prices ease.
Management expects Q2 growth in a similar band to Q1 despite a weaker July due to late rains; target is double-digit volume and value growth.
Strategic ambition: become number two in decorative and number one in industrial coatings, with a 2030-31 vision; decorative aim is market share gains while protecting absolute EBITDA.
Project Akshaya cost programme targets synergies with JSW Paints; ₹2.4 crore savings realised in Q1 and a 3-year roadmap set.
ERP migration from AkzoNobel systems planned by end of calendar year; TSA period is limited.
capex_capacity: Active towns about 3,400-3,500 out of 5,000+ presence; target to lift to about 4,500 this year, focusing on towns above 20,000 population.
Shift to direct/hybrid model in about the top 20 high-share towns; distributor model retained elsewhere.
Cross-manufacturing: JSW Paints made at Gwalior; JSW Dulux products made in JSW Paints plants; some JSW Paints products made in Mohali.
Headquarters moved from Delhi to JSW Centre, Mumbai during Q1.
demand_pricing: Volume growth ~25%, with price contributing ~6-7 points; growth driven by value per outlet from existing outlets, broadly secular across outlet types.
Gross-to-net reclassification of promotional spends (~2.5% of blended revenue) reduced reported gross margin; management says this aligns with industry presentation.
Management says decorative pricing has stabilised but competition from new entrants, with discounting, will persist for 1-2 years.

Discount ratio includes distributor commission (~4.5-4.7% of revenue), which management says makes dealer commissions otherwise modest; company benchmarks pricing to the market leader, not new entrants.
Benefit expected as high-priced inventory bought at end-March is consumed; lower-cost stock now entering August.

qa_highlights.question: What execution changes are driving better decorative performance, beyond headcount?
qa_highlights.answer: Micro-market segmentation by share tiers; reinforced Velvet Touch and WeatherShield; focus on undercoats such as primers in weak states; digital lead management, AI/analytics and an architect/painter programme. Hybrid direct model being tested in top 20 towns.

qa_highlights.question: How does volume-value gap reconcile with mix improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three factors: high-cost inventory, ~2.5% gross-to-net reclassification, and faster growth in lower-margin industrial and other businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Target for top-three position and inorganic plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined JSW Paints and JSW Dulux revenue is about ₹6,000 crore. Aim is to become number two; industrial to be number one in 1-1.5 years and wider ambition by 2030-31. No explicit M&A mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive intensity and discounting vs. new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition to remain intense for 1-2 years; company does not match new entrant discounts and benchmarks against the market leader.

qa_highlights.question: Decorative outperformance vs Asian Paints and Berger (8-9% volume growth)?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to premium-led growth, distribution expansion, digital tools and recovery in smaller dealers after new-entrant pressure; no single driver cited.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for July-August?
qa_highlights.answer: July was weaker due to late rains, but management expects Q2 in a similar band and targets double-digit growth in volume and value.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery to the 39.5-40% underlying level as high-cost inventory is consumed; crude-linked raw material costs.
EBITDA margin trajectory versus the 13-15% guidance as headcount and R&D costs continue.
Persistent discounting by new entrants in decorative; mass and economy segment growth lagging.
One-off income (₹55.9 crore dividend, ₹108 crore tax refund) inflates Q1 PAT; underlying profit is lower.
Execution risk in Project Akshaya, ERP migration and exit from AkzoNobel TSA; related-party governance with JSW Paints.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volume growth and market share ambitions, while openly explaining margin shortfall via inventory, reclassification and reinvestment. Somewhat evasive on specific M&A and the precise timeline for top-three positioning; cautious on competitive intensity.
key_quotes: we have decided to reinvest in the growth.
But given the crude prices, I have said that the EBITDA margin would be in the range of 13% to 15%.
Unless you grow 20% in decorative and volume, you can't get a 25% volume growth.
